items.title: Section: Sequence From Sunrise to Sunset, and Time Itself — Relative Even Among the Heavens

items.zh: 答：依一一行流轉分位，建立次第。此復三種。謂剎那流轉次第、內身流轉次第、成立所作流轉次第。問：依何分位建立時？此復幾種？答：依行相續不斷分位，建立時。此復三種。謂去、來、今。
items.en: Answer: sequence is established upon the orderly succession any process of conditioned arising displays. It is of three kinds: momentary sequence, the sequence of bodily activity, and the sequence of the physical universe's own original arrangement. Answer: time is established upon the stage of formations' uninterrupted continuity. It is of three kinds: past, future, and present.

items.zh: 問：依何分位建立方？此復幾種？

items.title: Section: Place in Three Directions, and Number Built From Nothing but Comparison

items.zh: 答：依所攝受諸色分位，建立方。此復三種。謂上、下、傍。問：依何分位建立數？此復幾種？答：依法齊量表了分位，建立數。此復三種。謂一數、二數、多數。
items.en: Answer: place is established upon the position occupied by the forms under consideration. It is of three kinds: above, below, and to the side. Answer: number is established upon whatever measure allows a phenomenon's quantity to be expressed. It is of three kinds: the singular, the dual, and the plural.

items.zh: 問：依何分位建立和合？此復幾種？

items.title: Section: Union and Disunion Close the List — Twenty-Four Factors That Are Neither Form Nor Mind, Fully Explained

items.zh: 答：依所作支無闕分位，建立和合。此復三種。謂集會和合、一義和合、圓滿和合。問：依何分位建立不和合？此復幾種？答：與和合相違，應知不和合若分位、若差別。
items.en: Answer: union is established upon the stage in which every necessary supporting condition is complete. It is of three kinds: union through gathering, through a single object, and through completion. Question: upon what basis is disunion established, and how many kinds are there? Answer: the exact reverse of union — its basis and its distinctions should be understood accordingly.

items.title: Section: Twenty-Nine Angles Begin — Which Aggregate Has Form, and Which Portion Can Actually Be Seen

items.zh: 問：於諸蘊中，何義、幾蘊是有色？答：即以此性還說此性，色自性義是有色義。一蘊是有色。問：何義、幾蘊是有見？答：眼所行義。一蘊一分是有見。
items.en: Question: among the aggregates, what does it mean to possess form, and how many aggregates qualify? Answer: form's own essential nature is precisely this meaning. One aggregate possesses form. Question: what does it mean to be visible, and how many aggregates qualify? Answer: being the domain of the eye's own activity. A portion of one aggregate is visible.

items.title: Section: Resistance, Contamination, and Affliction's Four Genuine Faults

items.zh: 答：展轉相觸據處所義及麁大義，是有對義。麁大義者，當知遠離三種微細。此三微細，如前應知。一蘊一分是有對。問：何義、幾蘊是有漏？答：麁重所隨，非彼對治煩惱所生義。一切一分是有漏。復有有漏義，謂若是處煩惱能生四種過失，是有漏義。何等名為四種過失？一、不寂靜過失，二、內外變異過失，三、發起惡行過失，四、攝受因過失。
items.en: Answer: mutual contact occupying space, and coarseness, together constitute resistance. A portion of one aggregate is resistant. Answer: being followed by affliction's own heaviness, not yet countered, and arising from affliction — this is the meaning of contamination. A portion of all five aggregates is contaminated. What are the four faults? Restlessness, internal and external alteration, generating unwholesome conduct, and serving as the cause that takes up a future rebirth.

items.zh: 當知初過失，纏現行所作；第二過失，諸煩惱事隨逐煩惱所作；第三過失，煩惱因緣所作；第四過失，引發後有所作。問：何義、幾蘊是有為？

items.title: Section: Conditioned, Contentious, Savoured, and Craved — Four Properties in Quick Succession

items.zh: 答：從因已生及應生義。一切是有為。問：何義、幾蘊是有諍？答：多隨瞋恚自在轉義。一切一分是有諍。問：何義、幾蘊是有愛味？答：多隨愛見自在轉義。一切一分是有愛味。問：何義、幾蘊是依耽嗜？答：多隨欲貪自在轉義。一切一分是依耽嗜。
items.en: Answer: already arisen from a cause, or destined to arise from one — all five aggregates are conditioned. Answer: largely governed by aversion's free operation — a portion of all five is contentious. Answer: largely governed by craving and view's free operation — a portion of all five possesses savour. Answer: largely governed by desire-realm craving's free operation — a portion of all five depends on craving.

items.title: Section: Worldliness, the Three Realms — And Why One Single Instant Already Contains Past, Present, and Future

items.zh: 答：戲論依義。一切一分是世間。問：何義、幾蘊是墮界？答：三界所攝世間義。一切一分是墮界。問：何義、幾蘊是過去？答：已受用因果義。一切是過去。問：何義、幾蘊是未來？答：未受用因果義。一切是未來。問：何義、幾蘊是現在？答：已受用因義及未受用果義。一切是現在。
items.en: Answer: serving as the basis for conceptual proliferation — a portion of all five is worldly. Answer: subsumed under the three realms as world — a portion of all five is confined to a realm. Answer: cause and effect already fully experienced — all five are past. Answer: not yet experienced — all five are future. Answer: cause already experienced, effect not yet — all five are present.

items.title: Section: Internal, External, Coarse, Subtle, Inferior, Excellent, Far, and Near — Eight Properties in Rapid Succession

items.zh: 答：六處并屬彼義。一蘊一分、四蘊全是內。問：何義、幾蘊是外？答：內相違義。一蘊一分是外。問：何義、幾蘊是麁？答：不光潔積聚相增長義。一切一分是麁。問：何義、幾蘊是細？答：麁相違義。一切一分是細。問：何義、幾蘊是劣？答：無常、苦、不淨、染污義。一切一分是劣。問：何義、幾蘊是妙？答：劣相違義。一切一分是妙。問：何義、幾蘊是遠？答：處所、去來、時、方隔越義。一切一分是遠。問：何義、幾蘊是近？答：遠相違義。一切一分是近。
items.en: Answer: the six sense faculties and what belongs to them — a portion of one aggregate and the whole of four are internal. Answer: the opposite of internal — a portion of one aggregate is external. Answer: lacking lustre, accumulated, ever-growing — a portion of all five is coarse; its opposite is subtle. Answer: impermanent, unsatisfactory, impure, defiled — a portion of all five is inferior; its opposite is excellent. Answer: separation in place and direction, or in the time of past and future — a portion of all five is distant; its opposite is near.

blocks.text: The list of dissociated formations ends with time, place, and number, and then the aggregates are examined from twenty-nine angles.
Master Cháng Bǎi: time is set upon the unbroken continuation of conditioned things, and so it too is provisional.
Place is set upon the positions of forms; number upon what expresses measure.
Master Cháng Bǎi: mind and factors together take one object; union is the stage in which the conditions for a task are complete.
Form's own nature is the meaning of "having form"; what the eye engages is "visible", a portion of one aggregate.

Mutual contact occupying space, and coarseness, constitute resistance. Master Cháng Bǎi: things connected with affliction are the body it depends on and the world it takes as object. (Untranslated, 0608a18: affliction's four faults are its manifest bonds, its following of afflictive things, its causes, and its drawing forth of a future life.)
Contention goes with aversion; savour with craving and view. Master Cháng Bǎi: when body, speech, and mind mostly follow aversion, they are "contentious".
The past: cause and effect fully experienced; the future: not yet; the present: cause experienced but effect not yet. Master Cháng Bǎi: the present aggregates are brought by past karma.
Master Cháng Bǎi: coarse and subtle exist by comparison, not as real differences.
"The present: the cause has been experienced, the result not yet." Each moment carries the past and seeds the future.

quiz.q: What are the three kinds of sequence?
options: the sequences of seeing, cultivation, and beyond learning, sequence concerning practice alone and not the world
above, below, and to the side
one, two, and many
momentary sequence, the sequence of the inner body, and the sequence of what is established
quiz.why: The treatise names three. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first is the moment-by-moment succession of phenomena; the third, following the Commentary, is the arrangement of the outer world at the start of the eon. The Sub-commentary reads the second as dependent origination and the third as household and monastic conduct, a reading the English does not mention.

quiz.q: The English has "the uninterrupted succession of cause and effect" for 依行相續不斷. What is the problem, given §10?
options: the Chinese says cause and effect in both, time and continuity being two names for one phenomenon
the Chinese says time is real, so "established" is wrong
the Chinese speaks of the seasons, which the English omits
the Chinese says 行 continue, not cause and effect; the wording matches §10's continuity, losing the difference between time and continuity
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the idea of time is set upon the unbroken continuation of conditioned phenomena, and so time too is provisional. §10 sets continuity upon cause and effect, while here the Chinese says 行. The English uses the same phrase in both, so a reader cannot see why the treatise has two different items.

quiz.q: How are place and number established, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: place is real space prior to form; number is a real phenomenon independent of things, so one and one always make two
place and number were both set by the Buddha
place upon the forms involved; number upon phenomena's mutual relation, both provisional
place rests on mind and number on form
quiz.why: The treatise sets place upon the forms involved, and number upon what expresses a phenomenon's measure. Master Cháng Bǎi: place is set upon the positions of inner and outer forms; number is set upon the relation of conditioned phenomena to one another. So neither space nor number is a separate reality.

quiz.q: The English has "union through shared purpose" for 一義和合. How does the lecture explain 一義?
options: 一義 is one aspiration, a community vowing to practise together, so "purpose" is exact and unrelated to objects
一義 is one object, mind and factors taking one object; "purpose" does not include this sense
一義 is one meaning, of words with the same sense
一義 is the ultimate truth
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 一義 is one object; mind and factors together take one object. Union itself is set upon the stage in which the conditions for a task are complete. "Shared purpose" could fit a group sharing an aim, but it does not reach the lecture's sense of a shared object of cognition.

quiz.q: What do "having form" and "visible" mean, and how many aggregates qualify?
options: the eye's domain is having form, one aggregate; form's nature is visible, all five, since all can be seen
form's own nature is having form, one aggregate; the eye's domain is visible, a portion of one
both are a portion of all five
having form is four aggregates; none are visible
quiz.why: The treatise says form's own nature is the meaning of having form, and one aggregate qualifies; what the eye engages is visible, a portion of one aggregate. Master Cháng Bǎi: the meaning of having form is explained by form's own characteristic. Visible means what the eye takes, only part of form, not sound or smell.

quiz.q: What is the definition of resistant, and how many aggregates qualify?
options: that which obstructs the noble path; all five aggregates, since all obstruct liberation
that which counters affliction; only wholesome factors
mutual contact occupying space, and coarseness; a portion of one aggregate, the ten material sense-bases
that which faces mind; all form and factors
quiz.why: The treatise says mutual contact occupying space, and coarseness, constitute resistance, and a portion of one aggregate qualifies. Master Cháng Bǎi: two phenomena that can touch one another and occupy space, and coarse form, are resistant; this portion is the ten material sense-bases of the form aggregate.

quiz.q: The English has "not yet countered" for 非彼對治. How do the Sub-commentary and the lecturer read it?
options: both read it as active, so the English reverses the voice and should be "not a remedy"
the Sub-commentary is active, this phenomenon does not counter affliction; the lecturer and English are passive, not yet countered; both should be noted
the Sub-commentary says this phenomenon is itself the remedy
both say the phrase has nothing to do with remedy
quiz.why: The Sub-commentary reads 非彼對治 as this phenomenon not being able to counter those afflictions, an active sense. Master Cháng Bǎi speaks of seeds of affliction before they have been countered, a passive sense, which the English follows. The two come to similar practical conclusions, but they differ in grammar, and a note would serve the reader.

quiz.q: Among contamination's four faults, how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain alteration and 攝受因?
options: outer things change by themselves, unrelated to affliction; 攝受因 means gathering disciples, the cause of a growing community
alteration is bodily illness; 攝受因 is food
things connected with affliction, the body and world, change with it; affliction brings a next ripened body, again joined with affliction
alteration is the world's formation and decay; 攝受因 is karmic seeds
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: things connected with affliction are the body on which it depends and the world it takes as object, which change according with it; and affliction brings about a next ripened body, joined again with affliction. The English "securing a future rebirth" turns 因, cause, into its result, though the sense is close.

quiz.q: Under whose free operation are contentious, savoured, and dependent on craving?
options: contentious, aversion; savoured, craving and view; dependent, desire-realm craving
contentious, desire-realm craving; savoured, aversion; dependent, craving and view, all three only in the desire realm
all three follow ignorance
all three follow wholesome aspiration
quiz.why: The treatise ties contentious to aversion, savoured to craving and view, and dependent on craving to desire-realm craving. Master Cháng Bǎi: when body, speech, and mind mostly follow aversion, they are contentious; desire-craving means the defiled mind towards the forms, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and sexes of the desire realm. The English has "craving" for three Chinese words.

quiz.q: Why does Master Cháng Bǎi say the three times are complete in one moment of the aggregates?
options: because the aggregates are timeless, past and future do not exist, and the three are names for one instant
because noble ones can see the three times
the present aggregates are brought by past karma, and present action at once infuses seeds, so they are past, present, and future together
because the aggregates are in three worlds at once
quiz.why: The treatise defines past as cause and effect fully experienced, future as not yet, and present as cause experienced but effect not. Master Cháng Bǎi: the present aggregates are brought by past karma, and present action at once infuses seeds; so one moment holds past, present, and future, and the treatise is nearly one great contemplation of no-self.

quiz.q: What are the meanings of worldly and confined to a realm?
options: worldly: the basis of proliferation; confined: subsumed under the three realms as world
worldly: subsumed under the three realms; confined: the basis of proliferation, both of identical range
worldly: the human world; confined: hell
worldly: the opposite of the supramundane; confined: losing powers
quiz.why: The treatise defines worldly as the basis of conceptual proliferation, and confined to a realm as subsumed under the three realms. Master Cháng Bǎi: the faculties and objects on which worldly proliferation arises are worldly; the worlds of beings, of the physical universe, and of the aggregates within the three realms are confined.

quiz.q: Is the difference of coarse and subtle a real one, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: coarse and subtle are two real classes, a coarse thing being coarse forever, unchanged by comparison, and so treated separately
coarse means poor and subtle rich
coarse and subtle exist by comparison, not really; form of the desire realm is opaque and so coarse
coarse means male and subtle female
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: form bound to the desire realm is not lustrous and is coarse form; coarse and subtle exist by comparison, not as real differences. The English "opaque" does not correspond closely to 不光潔, which means lacking lustre. Contemplating this helps loosen clinging to the body's appearance.

quiz.q: The English has "separation across space, time, or passage." How does the lecture divide distance?
options: only distance of time, place not counting, the aggregates all being present, so "space" is an addition to delete
into closeness and distance of relationship
into distance of place and of time; place-distance rests on the form aggregate; "passage" is unclear, and the overview mentions only past and future
into distance of earth and heaven
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: what is far off in location is distance of place, and this is established on the form aggregate. The Sub-commentary distinguishes it from distance of time. The English "space, time, or passage" has three terms for what the lecture groups in two, and the overview's conclusion mentions only past and future.
